mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cec4 disrupts the A. baumannii membrane and increases leakage of 260 nm-absorbing intracellular material in a dose/time-dependent assay.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Bacterial membrane disruption activity of Cec4; xml:fig=2:Figure 2

mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay supports membrane disruption, not a single molecular pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TEM images show progressive membrane/cell-wall damage after Cec4 treatment at 1x MIC.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Bacterial membrane disruption activity of Cec4; xml:fig=3:Figure 3

mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy is qualitative and time-point specific.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-Cec4 fluorescence/CLSM evidence supports bacterial association and intracellular entry over time.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Bacterial membrane disruption activity of Cec4; xml:fig=4:Figure 4; xml:supp=Figure S1

mechanism_claims.limitations: Localization supports entry/binding but does not identify a precise intracellular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: DNA-binding assay is negative; the paper reports Cec4 does not target DNA under the tested conditions.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=20:DNA-binding property and flow cytometry analysis; xml:supp=Figure S2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Negative plasmid-DNA binding does not exclude all intracellular targets.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Flow-cytometry evidence shows Cec4-treated A. baumannii accumulate more cells in G1-like phase after 30 min.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=20:DNA-binding property and flow cytometry analysis; xml:fig=5:Figure 5

mechanism_claims.limitations: Cell-cycle distribution is downstream phenotype and should not be overread as a primary molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cec4 inhibits and disrupts A. baumannii biofilms in crystal-violet and regrowth/eradication assays.
